newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia seeks China's blessing on Taiwan flights.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia seeks China's blessing on Taiwan flights.

text.p: Cambodia plans to send senior aviation officials to China to seek its blessing for regular flights between Phnom Penh and Taipei, a plan which had angered Beijing, the director of civil aviation said on Friday.
"The delegation might go on April 1st," said Keo Sophal.

He said the team, likely to include Aviation Undersecretary of State Pok Sam Ell and Royal Air Cambodge chairman Vichit Ith, would "ask permission" to open air links with Taiwan, which China regards as a renegade province.
Taiwan's EVA Airways announced Taipei-Phnom Penh service in February, saying the two countries had signed a direct air link agreement in December.
EVA said earlier this week that its inaugural flight to Phnom Penh's Pochentong Airport would be on April 10.
But Keo Sophal told Reuters the EVA flight "depends on the discussions between our delegation and the Chinese authorities."
Cambodian authorities would stress that the arrangement was purely commercial and had no political implications, he said.

Xavier d'Abzac, an aide to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, reiterated on Friday that Cambodia followed a "one-China" policy recognising Beijing as the sole legitimate Chinese government.
But, noting that Taiwan was one of the biggest investors in war-ravaged Cambodia, he added, "We welcome all Chinese investors."
The air link accord has angered China, which regards Taiwan as ineligible to enter into sovereign agreements with other countries.

Cambodia has no diplomatic ties with Taiwan but allows the island republic to maintain a trade office in Phnom Penh. Cambodia approved $80 million worth of investment from Taiwan in 1996, up from $18 million in 1995.
